title: Measuring and Modelling Delays in Robot Manipulators for Temporally Precise Control Using Machine Learning
authors: Thomas Timm Andersen | Heni Ben Amor | Nils Axel Andersen | Ole Ravn
finding: UR10 and KR5 sixx: externally mounted 8 kHz gyroscope separates commanded, mechanical and reported joint speed extrema. Authors report 33,500 trials per arm and average actuation of 2.5×8 ms and 7.5×12 ms respectively. Extrema alignment incorporates mechanical dynamics; the cited release link was unavailable.

title: New Method to Measure End-to-End Delay of Virtual Reality
finding: Two light sensors capture a moving physical luminance gradient and rendered counterpart on synchronous stereo inputs. Estimates motion-to-visual phase at different movement frequencies. This reference covers clock design and frequency dependence; its endpoint is emitted light.
rights: Public author version; reuse of source media unspecified; citation only.

title: Demonstration of Real-Time Event Camera to Collaborative Robot Communication
authors: Laura Duarte | Michele Polito | Laura Gastaldi | Pedro Neto | Stefano Pastorelli
locator: §§2–3, Fig. 4 and Table 1; arXiv v1 PDF p. 6
finding: Stepper-driven mock hand and UR3 elbow observed by two 200 Hz synchronized Opal gyros (<1 ms relative sync reported). Authors give 110 ms cross-correlation latency at 0.5 Hz. Figure-only estimates over the visible interval differ; event-camera/PC clocks were unsynchronized, leaving UDP and robot dynamics unresolved.
rights: arXiv v1 CC BY 4.0; derived pixel-lag summaries with attribution, no article or figure copied.

title: Robotic goalie with 3 ms reaction time at 4% CPU load using event-based dynamic vision sensor
finding: Flashed LED→controller pin median 2.2 ms; the servo power-supply drop indicating motor energization gives 5–15 ms including PWM phase. Independent visual tracking in one blocking event shows roughly 80 ms movement to position and overshoot. Current onset, movement and arrival are different observables.
rights: Open access CC BY; original summaries only.

title: Fast sensory motor control based on event-based hybrid neuromorphic-procedural system

rights: Author laboratory PDF; third-party reuse unspecified; citation only.
